🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Draft of COP31 cover text drops references to fossil fuel phase-out, net zero dates

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 01:01:16 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The latest iteration of the COP 31 draft cover text has eliminated references to fossil fuel phase-out and net-zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries. This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated. A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus. The COP31 Presidency’s revised draft cover decision, dated November 19, has 80 paragraphs, down from 144 in the November 16 version. The summit officially ends on November 20, though negotiations frequently overshoot into the weekend. A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated. However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, scaling up the use of carbon capture utilisation technologies and making early warning systems universal by 2027, continue to find mention in the text. A broad commitment to triple adaptation finance also remains. “ The draft cover text weaves the 35% electricity in final energy consumption by 2035, alongside tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling the rate of energy efficiency improvement by 2030, ” Ajay Mathur, India’s lead negotiator at Paris COP and former DG, International Solar Alliance, said in a statement. The electricity use in India went up by 13% in 2025 due to the Hormuz crisis alone. It will be an ambitious goal for India to achieve 35% electrification by 2035, but due to the increasing amount of renewable energy in the Indian energy mix, we will be near the 32-34% mark by 2035. ” “We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS) in a statement. “Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: United Nations / climate change / climate change (politics) / United Nations (climate change)

articles.title: Mahua Moitra alleges attack on her convoy by BJP supporters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: BJP leaders said the alleged attack was Ms. Moitra’s attempt to gain attention and conduct self-promotion through social media live videos

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Mamata All India Trinamool Congress lawmaker Mahua Moitra on Thursday (November 19, 2026) alleged that Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) members attacked her convoy when she was visiting her constituency — Krishnanagar — in Nadia district. She also accused the West Bengal police of inaction. It is not the first time that the MP has been attacked since the BJP came to power in the State. “I have been attacked by the mob, with police waiting. My car was physically lifted. I have seen the same BJP member [I recognise his face] with flags,” Ms. Moitra said in a video statement after her car was attacked and vandalised. She asked the Supreme Court, the Calcutta High Court, and the police to take note of the incident. The Mamata loyalist also shared videos of BJP flags being carried by the mob that allegedly attacked her car and threw eggs at the windscreen. Ms. Moitra alleged that instead of rescuing her and neutralising the mob, the police personnel tried to stop her from attending her scheduled event in the area. Meanwhile, Mamata's Trinamool general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and a Lok Sabha MP raised questions about the attack. “Will the Calcutta High Court initiate contempt proceedings against the State Government and the Home Department for defying its orders, or does contempt of court apply only to the Opposition while those in power and their BJP allies enjoy special immunity?” Mr Banerjee asked. West Bengal Industries Minister Tapas Roy said that without such incidents, Ms. Moitra does not get a chance to “go Live on Facebook”. “She (Mahua Moitra) wants self-promotion. Now she does not have any other way of promotion, so these incidents are the only way for her to get some attention. If she wants, she can inform the court about any such incident,” Mr. Roy said. On September 16, Ms. Moitra alleged that BJP workers pelted eggs on her during a visit to her Krishnanagar constituency in West Bengal’s Nadia.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mahua Moitra alleges attack by BJP workers at her constituency

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Mahua Moitra alleges attack on her convoy by BJP supporters

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 04:39:14 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: BJP leaders said the alleged attack was Ms. Moitra’s attempt to gain attention and conduct self-promotion through social media live videos

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Mamata All India Trinamool Congress lawmaker Mahua Moitra on Thursday (November 19, 2026) alleged that Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) members attacked her convoy when she was visiting her constituency — Krishnanagar — in Nadia district. She also accused the West Bengal police of inaction. It is not the first time that the MP has been attacked since the BJP came to power in the State. “I have been attacked by the mob, with police waiting. My car was physically lifted. I have seen the same BJP member [I recognise his face] with flags,” Ms. Moitra said in a video statement after her car was attacked and vandalised. She asked the Supreme Court, the Calcutta High Court, and the police to take note of the incident. The Mamata loyalist also shared videos of BJP flags being carried by the mob that allegedly attacked her car and threw eggs at the windscreen. Ms. Moitra alleged that instead of rescuing her and neutralising the mob, the police personnel tried to stop her from attending her scheduled event in the area. Meanwhile, Mamata's Trinamool general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and a Lok Sabha MP raised questions about the attack. “Will the Calcutta High Court initiate contempt proceedings against the State Government and the Home Department for defying its orders, or does contempt of court apply only to the Opposition while those in power and their BJP allies enjoy special immunity?” Mr Banerjee asked. West Bengal Industries Minister Tapas Roy said that without such incidents, Ms. Moitra does not get a chance to “go Live on Facebook”. “She (Mahua Moitra) wants self-promotion. Now she does not have any other way of promotion, so these incidents are the only way for her to get some attention. If she wants, she can inform the court about any such incident,” Mr. Roy said. On September 16, Ms. Moitra alleged that BJP workers pelted eggs on her during a visit to her Krishnanagar constituency in West Bengal’s Nadia.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mahua Moitra alleges attack by BJP workers at her constituency

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Opposition (Noun)
विरोध — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Opposition' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Attention (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Attention' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Action must be taken against such “dimagi naxals” who have conducted such activities inside the campus, said State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The violence at Medical College, Kolkata, on Wednesday evening has brought the West Bengal government and the Left student unions at loggerheads. A day after the violence, State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee on Thursday ordered an inquiry into the violence and said that a small group of students with “maoists and naxal mentality” were behind the incident and assaulted some senior faculty members of the medical college. Videos of the violence that has surfaced from the institution on Wednesday had revealed that ‘outsiders’ were pelting stones that damaged window panes and other infrastructure of the hospital. While a section of junior doctors had blamed Akhil Bharatiya Vidharthi Parishad for the violence, the student wing of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh denied any involvement in the violence. The Minister, however, put the blame on “ dimagi naxals", referring to the left student unions of the medical college. “The principal, vice-principal, and many senior authorities and professors of the college were manhandled and abused by the junior doctors inside the principal’s office. We have CCTV footage for every minute. Action must be taken against such “dimagi naxals” who have conducted such activities inside the campus,” Mr Mukherjee said. The Minister added that these are around 10-12 students who conducted this vandalism and have wrongfully claimed to “represent” the whole junior doctors and interns community. “We will not tolerate such hooliganism inside a hospital. We are keeping a watch on this. Medical College is not the place for communists to spread their anarchy,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said about the incident. The remarks by the Minister evoked strong reactions from the medical fraternity, including the Joint Platform of Doctors, which had held sustained protests after the rape and murder of a doctor at Kolkata’s R. G. Kar Hospital and Medical college in August 2024. The protests are considered one of the reasons that brought the downfall of the Mamata Banerjee government in May 2026. Representatives of the doctor’s association said that despite a change of the party in power, those occupying positions of prominence are behaving in a similar manner. Protests had started at the oldest medical college and hospital in the State after eight junior doctors had been sent a show-cause notice by the authorities on November 17, 2026 for allegedly holding a press conference over Chorbagan Durga Puja stampede last month. The junior doctors had raised questions on why the injured in the stampede were shifted to a private health facility.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Kolkata Medical College violence: West Bengal government, Left student’s unions at loggerheads

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 04:18:17 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Action must be taken against such “dimagi naxals” who have conducted such activities inside the campus, said State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The violence at Medical College, Kolkata, on Wednesday evening has brought the West Bengal government and the Left student unions at loggerheads. A day after the violence, State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee on Thursday ordered an inquiry into the violence and said that a small group of students with “maoists and naxal mentality” were behind the incident and assaulted some senior faculty members of the medical college. Videos of the violence that has surfaced from the institution on Wednesday had revealed that ‘outsiders’ were pelting stones that damaged window panes and other infrastructure of the hospital. While a section of junior doctors had blamed Akhil Bharatiya Vidharthi Parishad for the violence, the student wing of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh denied any involvement in the violence. The Minister, however, put the blame on “ dimagi naxals", referring to the left student unions of the medical college. “The principal, vice-principal, and many senior authorities and professors of the college were manhandled and abused by the junior doctors inside the principal’s office. We have CCTV footage for every minute. Action must be taken against such “dimagi naxals” who have conducted such activities inside the campus,” Mr Mukherjee said. The Minister added that these are around 10-12 students who conducted this vandalism and have wrongfully claimed to “represent” the whole junior doctors and interns community. “We will not tolerate such hooliganism inside a hospital. We are keeping a watch on this. Medical College is not the place for communists to spread their anarchy,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said about the incident. The remarks by the Minister evoked strong reactions from the medical fraternity, including the Joint Platform of Doctors, which had held sustained protests after the rape and murder of a doctor at Kolkata’s R. G. Kar Hospital and Medical college in August 2024. The protests are considered one of the reasons that brought the downfall of the Mamata Banerjee government in May 2026. Representatives of the doctor’s association said that despite a change of the party in power, those occupying positions of prominence are behaving in a similar manner. Protests had started at the oldest medical college and hospital in the State after eight junior doctors had been sent a show-cause notice by the authorities on November 17, 2026 for allegedly holding a press conference over Chorbagan Durga Puja stampede last month. The junior doctors had raised questions on why the injured in the stampede were shifted to a private health facility.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: After the show cause notice, several junior doctors started a sit-in demonstration inside the campus and gheraoed the principal inside his room.

✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
Demonstration (Adjective / Verb)
प्रदर्शन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Demonstration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Involvement (Adjective)
भागीदारी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Involvement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Kolkata Medical College violence: West Bengal government, Left student’s unions at loggerheads", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Action must be taken against such “dimagi naxals” who have conducted such activities inside the campus, said State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Kolkata Medical College violence: West Bengal go' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Kolkata Medical College violence: West Bengal' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Kolkata Medical College violence: West Bengal' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Action must be taken against such “dimagi naxals” who have conducted such activities inside the campus, said State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Kolkata Medical College violence: West Bengal government, Left student’s unions at loggerheads"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. After the show cause notice, several junior doctors started a sit-in demonstration inside the campus and gheraoed the principal inside his room.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "After the show cause notice, several junior doctors started a sit-in demonstration inside the campus and gheraoed the principal inside his room." (Hinglish Arth: कारण बताओ नोटिस के बाद कई जूनियर डॉक्टरों ने परिसर में धरना-प्रदर्शन शुरू कर दिया और प्राचार्य का उनके कक्ष में ही घेराव कर लिया.)

articles.title: Video of Bihar CM’s security ‘pushing’ Nishant sparks row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Alliance partner Janata Dal (United) objected strongly, saying the Assembly mandate was in Nitish Kumar’s name. The party demanded action, calling it an insult to Nishant and all its workers

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A row erupted in Bihar on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after a video went viral on social media purportedly showing a security officer of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary ‘pushing’ State Health Minister Nishant Kumar. The incident took place in Vaishali district on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) when both leaders went to inspect the venue that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit on November 21 to inaugurate a six-lane bridge named after Mr. Nishant’s father and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. Janata Dal (United) [JD(U)] MLC and chief spokesperson Neeraj Kumar raised a strong objection over the incident and demanded that the Bihar police investigate the matter and find out whether it was done intentionally or inadvertently. He also termed the video “disturbing and painful”. “Nishant Kumar is the Minister in-charge of Vaishali district and had gone with the Chief Minister,” Mr. Neeraj told reporters at his official residence in Patna. The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) also took a dig at the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government by sharing the video on X. “As soon as poor Nitish Kumar fell ill and became unconscious, the BJP first snatched his Chief Minister’s post. Now, poor Nitish is having his son pushed around by the BJP’s CM police officers,” the RJD said. RJD Chief Lalu Prasad’s daughter, Rohini Acharya, also posted the video on X and asked, “Why are Uncle Nitish Kumar and brother Nishant Kumar being forced to endure humiliation?” “First, Nitish Kumar was sidelined in a humiliating manner, and now the BJP is publicly humiliating his son Nishant. It seems Nitish ji has completely buried his self-respect and dignity, and now he is forcing his son to fall in line with his own ways too,” Ms. Acharya wrote in the post Asked about any possibility of the RJD and the JD(U) coming together once again, Leader of the Opposition and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav said, “I do now know what people are talking about, but whatever I had said before the election, everything is coming true. I had said the BJP will not allow Nitishji to remain in the CM’s post, it has happened.” He further said, “JD(U) is no longer united; it has become divided. For their own vested interests and comfort, Sanjay Jha and Lalan Singh took Nitish Ji to the BJP. They want to finish JD(U); that’s why Nishant is not made Deputy Chief Minister. Forget Deputy CM—if Nitish Ji were CM, Nishant would also have been made CM. If Nitish Ji were in a conscious state, he would have been in Mahagathbandhan .”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A few days ago, RJD MP from Aurangabad, Abhay Kushwaha, said that Lalu Prasad and Tejashwi would welcome Nitish if he wishes to return to the Mahagathbandhan . Mr. Kushwaha went on to say that if Nitish wishes, his son could be made Chief Minister.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Video of Bihar CM’s security ‘pushing’ Nishant sparks row

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 04:03:42 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Alliance partner Janata Dal (United) objected strongly, saying the Assembly mandate was in Nitish Kumar’s name. The party demanded action, calling it an insult to Nishant and all its workers

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A row erupted in Bihar on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after a video went viral on social media purportedly showing a security officer of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary ‘pushing’ State Health Minister Nishant Kumar. The incident took place in Vaishali district on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) when both leaders went to inspect the venue that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit on November 21 to inaugurate a six-lane bridge named after Mr. Nishant’s father and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. Janata Dal (United) [JD(U)] MLC and chief spokesperson Neeraj Kumar raised a strong objection over the incident and demanded that the Bihar police investigate the matter and find out whether it was done intentionally or inadvertently. He also termed the video “disturbing and painful”. “Nishant Kumar is the Minister in-charge of Vaishali district and had gone with the Chief Minister,” Mr. Neeraj told reporters at his official residence in Patna. The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) also took a dig at the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government by sharing the video on X. “As soon as poor Nitish Kumar fell ill and became unconscious, the BJP first snatched his Chief Minister’s post. Now, poor Nitish is having his son pushed around by the BJP’s CM police officers,” the RJD said. RJD Chief Lalu Prasad’s daughter, Rohini Acharya, also posted the video on X and asked, “Why are Uncle Nitish Kumar and brother Nishant Kumar being forced to endure humiliation?” “First, Nitish Kumar was sidelined in a humiliating manner, and now the BJP is publicly humiliating his son Nishant. It seems Nitish ji has completely buried his self-respect and dignity, and now he is forcing his son to fall in line with his own ways too,” Ms. Acharya wrote in the post Asked about any possibility of the RJD and the JD(U) coming together once again, Leader of the Opposition and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav said, “I do now know what people are talking about, but whatever I had said before the election, everything is coming true. I had said the BJP will not allow Nitishji to remain in the CM’s post, it has happened.” He further said, “JD(U) is no longer united; it has become divided. For their own vested interests and comfort, Sanjay Jha and Lalan Singh took Nitish Ji to the BJP. They want to finish JD(U); that’s why Nishant is not made Deputy Chief Minister. Forget Deputy CM—if Nitish Ji were CM, Nishant would also have been made CM. If Nitish Ji were in a conscious state, he would have been in Mahagathbandhan .”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A few days ago, RJD MP from Aurangabad, Abhay Kushwaha, said that Lalu Prasad and Tejashwi would welcome Nitish if he wishes to return to the Mahagathbandhan . Mr. Kushwaha went on to say that if Nitish wishes, his son could be made Chief Minister.

संभावना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Possibility' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

A. Alliance partner Janata Dal (United) objected strongly, saying the Assembly mandate was in Nitish Kumar’s name.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Video of Bihar CM’s security ‘pushing’ Nishant s' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Video of Bihar CM’s security ‘pushing’ Nishan' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Video of Bihar CM’s security ‘pushing’ Nishan' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Video of Bihar CM’s security ‘pushing’ Nishant sparks row"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Kushwaha went on to say that if Nitish wishes, his son could be made Chief Minister.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Kushwaha went on to say that if Nitish wishes, his son could be made Chief Minister." articles.title: Rajasthan High Court denies interim stay in IAS officer corruption probe
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The ACB has alleged that IAS officer Agarwal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates, and special concessional packages to the firm

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Rajasthan High Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) declined to grant an interim stay on the investigation launched against senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Shikhar Agarwal in a case of alleged corruption involving the purchase of 40 villas in luxury resorts operated by a private firm in the Udaipur and Alwar districts. Mr. Agarwal, who was placed on awaiting posting order (APO) last month, has challenged the State Government’s permission to the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) to conduct an enquiry against him under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. While the IAS officer sought protection against punitive action during the pendency of his petition, Justice Anil Kumar Upman directed the State Government to respond within three weeks to the plea. Mr. Agarwal is facing charges of abusing his position and influence and extending “undue benefits” to the firm. The alleged purchases of villas were made in the names of Mr. Agarwal, his wife, and Indian Police Service (IPS) officer Prashakha Mathur, their two sons, and Mr. Agarwal’s parents-in-law. The ACB has alleged that Mr. Agarwal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates, and special concessional packages to the firm. Based on the findings of the preliminary enquiry, the ACB registered a first information report on November 18 against Mr. Agarwal, directors of Goyal Fashions Private Limited, and others. A 1993-batch IAS officer, Mr. Agarwal was serving as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries) and was additionally holding charge of four public sector corporations. The petition contended that the approval for ACB’s probe was issued in “undue haste” without giving Mr. Agarwal an opportunity to explain his position. His counsel also disputed the description of the properties as villas, contending that they were rooms within villa complexes. The ACB has stated that Mr. Agarwal and his family members purchased the villas and cottages for approximately Rs. 6.17 crore and subsequently leased them back to the seller for an annual rent of around ₹1.80 crore.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rajasthan / corruption & bribery / crime / crime, law and justice

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Rajasthan High Court denies interim stay in IAS officer corruption probe

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 03:38:18 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The ACB has alleged that IAS officer Agarwal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates, and special concessional packages to the firm

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Rajasthan High Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) declined to grant an interim stay on the investigation launched against senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Shikhar Agarwal in a case of alleged corruption involving the purchase of 40 villas in luxury resorts operated by a private firm in the Udaipur and Alwar districts. Mr. Agarwal, who was placed on awaiting posting order (APO) last month, has challenged the State Government’s permission to the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) to conduct an enquiry against him under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. While the IAS officer sought protection against punitive action during the pendency of his petition, Justice Anil Kumar Upman directed the State Government to respond within three weeks to the plea. Mr. Agarwal is facing charges of abusing his position and influence and extending “undue benefits” to the firm. The alleged purchases of villas were made in the names of Mr. Agarwal, his wife, and Indian Police Service (IPS) officer Prashakha Mathur, their two sons, and Mr. Agarwal’s parents-in-law. The ACB has alleged that Mr. Agarwal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates, and special concessional packages to the firm. Based on the findings of the preliminary enquiry, the ACB registered a first information report on November 18 against Mr. Agarwal, directors of Goyal Fashions Private Limited, and others. A 1993-batch IAS officer, Mr. Agarwal was serving as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries) and was additionally holding charge of four public sector corporations. The petition contended that the approval for ACB’s probe was issued in “undue haste” without giving Mr. Agarwal an opportunity to explain his position. His counsel also disputed the description of the properties as villas, contending that they were rooms within villa complexes. The ACB has stated that Mr. Agarwal and his family members purchased the villas and cottages for approximately Rs. 6.17 crore and subsequently leased them back to the seller for an annual rent of around ₹1.80 crore.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rajasthan / corruption & bribery / crime / crime, law and justice

नियमों में ढील या छूट — किसी कड़े प्रतिबंध को थोड़े समय के लिए हल्का करना।
✓ Syn: Moderation, Easing, Leniency  |  ✖ Ant: Strictness, Tightening, Rigidity
Permissibility (Noun)
कानूनी अनुमति या स्वीकार्यता — किसी कार्य को करने की वैध छूट।
✓ Syn: Admissibility, Legality, Allowance  |  ✖ Ant: Prohibition, Ban, Illegality
Administrative (Adjective)
प्रशासनिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administrative' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Investigation (Adjective / Verb)
जाँच पड़ताल — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Investigation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Rajasthan High Court denies interim stay in IAS officer corruption probe", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The ACB has alleged that IAS officer Agarwal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Rajasthan High Court denies interim stay in IAS ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Rajasthan High Court denies interim stay in I' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Rajasthan High Court denies interim stay in I' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Rajasthan High Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) declined to grant an interim stay on the investigation launched against senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Shikhar Agarwal in a case of alleged corruption involving the purchase of 40 villas in luxury resorts operated by a private firm in the Udaipur and Alwar districts. While the IAS officer sought protection against punitive action during the pendency of his petition, Justice Anil Kumar Upman directed the State Government to respond within three weeks to the plea. Mr. Agarwal is facing charges of abusing his position and influence and extending “undue benefits” to the firm. The alleged purchases of villas were made in the names of Mr. Agarwal, his wife, and Indian Police Service (IPS) officer Prashakha Mathur, their two sons, and Mr. Agarwal’s parents-in-law. The ACB has alleged that Mr. Agarwal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates, and special concessional packages to the firm. Based on the findings of the preliminary enquiry, the ACB registered a first information report on November 18 against Mr. Agarwal, directors of Goyal Fashions Private Limited, and others. A 1993-batch IAS officer, Mr. Agarwal was serving as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries) and was additionally holding charge of four public sector corporations. The petition contended that the approval for ACB’s probe was issued in “undue haste” without giving Mr. Agarwal an opportunity to explain his position. His counsel also disputed the description of the properties as villas, contending that they were rooms within villa complexes. The ACB has stated that Mr. Agarwal and his family members purchased the villas and cottages for approximately Rs. 6.17 crore and subsequently leased them back to the seller for an annual rent of around ₹1.80 crore.

articles.title: Emerging radicalisation hotspots now under purview of Multi-Agency Centre: Amit Shah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Union Home Minister calls on anti-terrorism squads of every State to strengthen their cyber-expert units

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Multi-Agency Centre (MAC), a centralised intelligence-sharing platform, now tracks cybersecurity, narcotics, organised crime networks, and emerging radicalisation hotspots, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday (November 19, 2026). The MAC, which also acts as a common counter-terrorism grid and functions under the Intelligence Bureau (IB), was conceptualised in 2001, in the aftermath of the Kargil war, but became fully operational in 2009. In 2025, the MAC network was revamped to connect all police districts in the country through a secure network. Mr. Shah said that the functioning of the MAC has been reorganised. He said that the anti-terrorism squads (ATS) of every State needed to strengthen their cyber-expert units as technology is increasingly being used in such crimes. He made the remarks while addressing the inaugural session of the two-day counter-terrorism conference organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in New Delhi. On the occasion, he released the publication, Fail-Safe Investigation, brought out by the NIA. He also laid the foundation stone for the NIA’s office complex in Chandigarh and inaugurated the NIA’s residential complex at Maidangarhi in Delhi. In addition, the Union Home Minister e-launched the NIA’s ‘Pushti’ portal and conferred decorations on seven officers and personnel of the agency. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Intelligence Bureau Director Mahesh Dixit, Special Secretary (Internal Security) in the Ministry of Home Affairs, Anand Swarup, and NIA Director General Rakesh Aggarwal were present at the event. Mr. Shah said that India has been confronting terrorism for a long time, and noted that while the police forces of different States had made various kinds of efforts, a lack of coordinated action was clearly visible. Over time, during the tenures of successive governments, gradual efforts were made to overcome these shortcomings, he said. “Today, we can say with satisfaction that in this vast country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya — we are putting in place a system under which a uniform strategy to combat terrorism will operate right down to the level of every police station,” the Home Minister said. He said that with the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist Latif Bhat, Kashmir has become free from the presence of India-born terrorists, adding that this situation has come about after 35 years. He also said that more than 40 modules of the Shahzad Bhatti network, which has been declared a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), have been neutralised across the country.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Shah said that the hallmark of a successful agency is apprehending terrorists and putting them behind bars before they can carry out their plans. He said the police in every State should analyse this model and implement it in their respective areas.

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Emerging radicalisation hotspots now under purview of Multi-Agency Centre: Amit Shah

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 06:46:15 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Union Home Minister calls on anti-terrorism squads of every State to strengthen their cyber-expert units

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Multi-Agency Centre (MAC), a centralised intelligence-sharing platform, now tracks cybersecurity, narcotics, organised crime networks, and emerging radicalisation hotspots, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday (November 19, 2026). The MAC, which also acts as a common counter-terrorism grid and functions under the Intelligence Bureau (IB), was conceptualised in 2001, in the aftermath of the Kargil war, but became fully operational in 2009. In 2025, the MAC network was revamped to connect all police districts in the country through a secure network. Mr. Shah said that the functioning of the MAC has been reorganised. He said that the anti-terrorism squads (ATS) of every State needed to strengthen their cyber-expert units as technology is increasingly being used in such crimes. He made the remarks while addressing the inaugural session of the two-day counter-terrorism conference organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in New Delhi. On the occasion, he released the publication, Fail-Safe Investigation, brought out by the NIA. He also laid the foundation stone for the NIA’s office complex in Chandigarh and inaugurated the NIA’s residential complex at Maidangarhi in Delhi. In addition, the Union Home Minister e-launched the NIA’s ‘Pushti’ portal and conferred decorations on seven officers and personnel of the agency. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Intelligence Bureau Director Mahesh Dixit, Special Secretary (Internal Security) in the Ministry of Home Affairs, Anand Swarup, and NIA Director General Rakesh Aggarwal were present at the event. Mr. Shah said that India has been confronting terrorism for a long time, and noted that while the police forces of different States had made various kinds of efforts, a lack of coordinated action was clearly visible. Over time, during the tenures of successive governments, gradual efforts were made to overcome these shortcomings, he said. “Today, we can say with satisfaction that in this vast country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya — we are putting in place a system under which a uniform strategy to combat terrorism will operate right down to the level of every police station,” the Home Minister said. articles.title: Women in high public office doesn’t mean equality throughout society: Justice Nagarathna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Supreme Court judge says a woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Justice B.V. Nagarathna, one of the senior most judges of the Supreme Court and in line to be the first woman Chief Justice of India, has said that the mere existence of women in high public office does not establish that equality has been achieved throughout society. “A woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies,” Justice Nagarathna said at the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Somerville College in the University of Oxford on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Only the practice of substantive equality could take care of these differences among women hailing from and living through diverse life experiences, the judge said. Justice Nagarathna said a judgment cannot, by itself, guarantee that every workplace becomes safe, every girl receives education, every woman obtains her lawful inheritance, or every victim of domestic violence secures timely protection. Likewise, legislation cannot achieve its full purpose if remedies were inaccessible, public authorities failed to act, or social attitudes prevent women from asserting their rights. The judge said the enactment of Constitutional amendments which give women one-third of the seats in Parliament and the State legislatures was proof to show that women should participate in decision-making and not be content with just a formal right to vote. “These developments reflect an important insight: where historical exclusion has shaped the composition of institutions, formal equality alone may not be sufficient to secure meaningful representation,” Justice Nagarathna pointed out. Justice Nagarathna said that the progress of Indian women’s rights cannot be measured by the number of discriminatory provisions struck down or the enactment of a few beneficial laws. The judge said recognition of violence against women as a violation of constitutional rights has not really translated in the real world to women seeking the protection of law without fear of stigma, retaliation or economic insecurity.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On the question of equality, Justice Nagarathna raised the fundamental problem of women being made to bear the “disproportionate burden of unpaid domestic and care work which continues to determine women’s choices”.

hinglishTracks.en: On the question of equality, Justice Nagarathna raised the fundamental problem of women being made to bear the “disproportionate burden of unpaid domestic and care work which continues to determine women’s choices”.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — समानता के सवाल पर, न्यायमूर्ति नागरत्ना ने महिलाओं को "अवैतनिक घरेलू और देखभाल कार्यों का असंगत बोझ" वहन करने की मूलभूत समस्या उठाई, जो महिलाओं की पसंद को निर्धारित करना जारी रखती है।।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Women in high public office doesn’t mean equality throughout society: Justice Nagarathna

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 06:34:27 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Supreme Court judge says a woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Justice B.V. Nagarathna, one of the senior most judges of the Supreme Court and in line to be the first woman Chief Justice of India, has said that the mere existence of women in high public office does not establish that equality has been achieved throughout society. “A woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies,” Justice Nagarathna said at the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Somerville College in the University of Oxford on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Only the practice of substantive equality could take care of these differences among women hailing from and living through diverse life experiences, the judge said. Justice Nagarathna said a judgment cannot, by itself, guarantee that every workplace becomes safe, every girl receives education, every woman obtains her lawful inheritance, or every victim of domestic violence secures timely protection. Likewise, legislation cannot achieve its full purpose if remedies were inaccessible, public authorities failed to act, or social attitudes prevent women from asserting their rights. The judge said the enactment of Constitutional amendments which give women one-third of the seats in Parliament and the State legislatures was proof to show that women should participate in decision-making and not be content with just a formal right to vote. “These developments reflect an important insight: where historical exclusion has shaped the composition of institutions, formal equality alone may not be sufficient to secure meaningful representation,” Justice Nagarathna pointed out. Justice Nagarathna said that the progress of Indian women’s rights cannot be measured by the number of discriminatory provisions struck down or the enactment of a few beneficial laws. The judge said recognition of violence against women as a violation of constitutional rights has not really translated in the real world to women seeking the protection of law without fear of stigma, retaliation or economic insecurity.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On the question of equality, Justice Nagarathna raised the fundamental problem of women being made to bear the “disproportionate burden of unpaid domestic and care work which continues to determine women’s choices”.

Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Representation (Noun)
प्रतिनिधित्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Representation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Substantive (Adjective)
मूल — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Substantive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: Landfall process begins
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts early on Friday, says the India Meteorological Department (IMD). “Latest satellite imagery indicates the land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts,” informed IMD on Friday (November 20, 2026). The Severe Cyclonic Storm "Akvan" [Pronunciation: Akvan] over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 21 kmph during past 06 hours, weakened into a Cyclonic Storm and lay centered at 0230 hours IST of today, the 20th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 17.7°N and Longitude 84.9°E, about 110 km southeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 170 km east of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 170 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha), 250 km south-southwest of Puri (Odisha) and 370 km east-northeast of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh). It is likely to continue to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur, by forenoon of 20th November, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph. Latest Satellite imagery indicates the Land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the Cyclonic Storm "Akvan" entered into north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts. The system is under continuous surveillance of the Doppler Weather Radar at Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur. “The severe cyclonic storm Akvan over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 21 kmph during the past six hours, weakened into a cyclonic storm and lay centred over the same region about 110 km southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 170 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 250 km south-southwest of Puri (Odisha),” informed the IMD bulletin. “It is likely to continue to move north-northwestward and cross the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by the forenoon of November 20, 2026, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph,” it further said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours. Meanwhile, coastal Odisha districts have started receiving heavy rain under the influence of the cyclone.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Cyclone Akvan: Landfall process begins

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 06:33:55 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts early on Friday, says the India Meteorological Department (IMD). “Latest satellite imagery indicates the land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts,” informed IMD on Friday (November 20, 2026). The Severe Cyclonic Storm "Akvan" [Pronunciation: Akvan] over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 21 kmph during past 06 hours, weakened into a Cyclonic Storm and lay centered at 0230 hours IST of today, the 20th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 17.7°N and Longitude 84.9°E, about 110 km southeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 170 km east of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 170 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha), 250 km south-southwest of Puri (Odisha) and 370 km east-northeast of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh). It is likely to continue to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur, by forenoon of 20th November, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph. Latest Satellite imagery indicates the Land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the Cyclonic Storm "Akvan" entered into north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts. The system is under continuous surveillance of the Doppler Weather Radar at Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur. “The severe cyclonic storm Akvan over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 21 kmph during the past six hours, weakened into a cyclonic storm and lay centred over the same region about 110 km southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 170 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 250 km south-southwest of Puri (Odisha),” informed the IMD bulletin. “It is likely to continue to move north-northwestward and cross the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by the forenoon of November 20, 2026, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph,” it further said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours. Meanwhile, coastal Odisha districts have started receiving heavy rain under the influence of the cyclone.

सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Surveillance (Noun)
निगरानी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Surveillance' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

A. Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Cyclone Akvan: Landfall process begins' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Cyclone Akvan: Landfall process begins' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Cyclone Akvan: Landfall process begins' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

B. Meanwhile, coastal Odisha districts have started receiving heavy rain under the influence of the cyclone.

articles.title: Madhya Pradesh scraps two-child policy for Govt employees after 25 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The policy had been introduced in 2001 by the Congress government led by the then Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh as measure to check population rise

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet has approved scrapping of the 25-year-old two-child restriction policy for government employees and job aspirants while citing the declining birth rate in the country and in the State as the reason. The decision was taken on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at a special Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav at Gandhi Sagar Forest Retreat in Mandsaur district, where the removal of the provision and the related clarification concerning ‘more than two living children’ from the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services Rule was approved. The policy had been introduced in 2001 by the Congress government led by the then Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh as measure to check population rise. Under the rule, serving government employees faced disciplinary action upon having a third child while those who had more than two children were ineligible for government jobs. Addressing the press persons after the meet, Mr. Yadav said that the restriction caused many difficulties to government employees. “We have removed the restriction. This will bring major relief to government employees. When the rest of the society has no such restriction, then why should we put the government workers into trouble?” Mr. Yadav said. In a statement, the government said, “The Cabinet approved the removal of Sub-rule (6) of Rule 6 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1961. It also approved the deletion of the clarification concerning ‘more than two living children’ mentioned in Sub-rule (4) of Rule 22 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965.” The government said that the long-awaited decision was taken keeping in mind the falling fertility rates in the State as well as in the country. As a result of the move, it said, all ongoing disciplinary proceedings against government employees, that were initiated solely on the ground of having more than two living children, will be terminated with immediate effect. However, the case in which final orders have already been passed and penalties imposed through disciplinary proceedings will not be reopened.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) government’s decision is also being seen aligning with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)’s long-standing concern about lower fertility rates among the Hindu community compared to the Muslims. The RSS describes this as a “demographic imbalance” with various its affiliated bodies having passed resolutions urging the Centre and State governments to formulate a uniform national population policy applicable to all communities.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Madhya Pradesh scraps two-child policy for Govt employees after 25 years

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 07:17:45 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The policy had been introduced in 2001 by the Congress government led by the then Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh as measure to check population rise

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet has approved scrapping of the 25-year-old two-child restriction policy for government employees and job aspirants while citing the declining birth rate in the country and in the State as the reason. The decision was taken on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at a special Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav at Gandhi Sagar Forest Retreat in Mandsaur district, where the removal of the provision and the related clarification concerning ‘more than two living children’ from the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services Rule was approved. The policy had been introduced in 2001 by the Congress government led by the then Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh as measure to check population rise. Under the rule, serving government employees faced disciplinary action upon having a third child while those who had more than two children were ineligible for government jobs. Addressing the press persons after the meet, Mr. Yadav said that the restriction caused many difficulties to government employees. “We have removed the restriction. This will bring major relief to government employees. When the rest of the society has no such restriction, then why should we put the government workers into trouble?” Mr. Yadav said. In a statement, the government said, “The Cabinet approved the removal of Sub-rule (6) of Rule 6 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1961. It also approved the deletion of the clarification concerning ‘more than two living children’ mentioned in Sub-rule (4) of Rule 22 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965.” The government said that the long-awaited decision was taken keeping in mind the falling fertility rates in the State as well as in the country. As a result of the move, it said, all ongoing disciplinary proceedings against government employees, that were initiated solely on the ground of having more than two living children, will be terminated with immediate effect. However, the case in which final orders have already been passed and penalties imposed through disciplinary proceedings will not be reopened.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) government’s decision is also being seen aligning with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)’s long-standing concern about lower fertility rates among the Hindu community compared to the Muslims. The RSS describes this as a “demographic imbalance” with various its affiliated bodies having passed resolutions urging the Centre and State governments to formulate a uniform national population policy applicable to all communities.

articles.title: U.S. religious freedom panel says India is targeting minorities in voter roll revisions
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India has escalated its targeting of religious minorities ‌during a voter list revision that struck off tens of millions ​of names nationwide, a U.S. panel on religious freedom said on ⁠Thursday (November 19, 2026). “The Indian gov’t is targeting Muslim citizens by removing them from voter rolls, calling them ‘foreigners,’ and now illegally deporting them,” Asif Mahmood, the chair of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, ‌said in a statement. India’s voter list revision removed 130 million names, roughly the population of Mexico, in the largest deletion of voters in the ‌country’s history. Data shows the omissions disproportionately affect Muslims , India’s largest minority, who ‌have ⁠faced what rights groups describe as exclusionary policies and rising discrimination since Prime ⁠Minister Narendra Modi took power in 2014. The Election Commission of India says it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can pursue ​appeals. The revision has become entangled with ‌a separate drive to identify and expel suspected illegal immigrants, even though removal from the rolls does not itself establish that someone is a foreigner. “The Indian government’s expulsion of its own citizens based on their Muslim faith is a shocking ‌escalation of tactics that target religious minorities,” said Gene Mills, a commissioner ​on the U.S. panel. Mr. Mills urged the State Department to designate India as a “country of particular concern.” USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding. Washington has not acted on its recent recommendations on India.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Ministry of External Affairs has cast USCIRF as biased. New Delhi has repeatedly dismissed such criticism and called it interference in the country’s internal affairs. The Indian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 U.S. religious freedom panel says India is targeting minorities in voter roll revisions

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 07:07:32 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India has escalated its targeting of religious minorities ‌during a voter list revision that struck off tens of millions ​of names nationwide, a U.S. panel on religious freedom said on ⁠Thursday (November 19, 2026). “The Indian gov’t is targeting Muslim citizens by removing them from voter rolls, calling them ‘foreigners,’ and now illegally deporting them,” Asif Mahmood, the chair of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, ‌said in a statement. India’s voter list revision removed 130 million names, roughly the population of Mexico, in the largest deletion of voters in the ‌country’s history. Data shows the omissions disproportionately affect Muslims , India’s largest minority, who ‌have ⁠faced what rights groups describe as exclusionary policies and rising discrimination since Prime ⁠Minister Narendra Modi took power in 2014. The Election Commission of India says it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can pursue ​appeals. The revision has become entangled with ‌a separate drive to identify and expel suspected illegal immigrants, even though removal from the rolls does not itself establish that someone is a foreigner. “The Indian government’s expulsion of its own citizens based on their Muslim faith is a shocking ‌escalation of tactics that target religious minorities,” said Gene Mills, a commissioner ​on the U.S. panel. Mr. Mills urged the State Department to designate India as a “country of particular concern.” USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding. Washington has not acted on its recent recommendations on India.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Ministry of External Affairs has cast USCIRF as biased. New Delhi has repeatedly dismissed such criticism and called it interference in the country’s internal affairs. The Indian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.

Discrimination (Adjective / Verb)
भेदभाव — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Discrimination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Interference (Adjective / Verb)
दखल अंदाजी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Interference' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Commission (Noun)
आयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Commission' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "U.S. religious freedom panel says India is targeting minorities in voter roll revisions", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'U.S. religious freedom panel says India is targe' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'U.S. religious freedom panel says India is ta' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'U.S. religious freedom panel says India is ta' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S." (Hinglish Arth: यूएससीआईआरएफ अमेरिका का एक द्विदलीय निकाय है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "U.S. religious freedom panel says India is targeting minorities in voter roll revisions"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The Indian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The Indian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment." (Hinglish Arth: वाशिंगटन में भारतीय दूतावास ने टिप्पणी के अनुरोध का जवाब नहीं दिया।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again. That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: World / Ukraine / USA / Russia-Ukraine Crisis / war / war
